newsitem.title: USA: Global chip sales seen up 4.6 percent to $138 billion.
newsitem.headline: Global chip sales seen up 4.6 percent to $138 billion.

text.p: The global chip industry is projected to grow by 4.6 percent in 1997 to $138 billion, weighed down by a flat first quarter, with the yearly growth rate then spiking above 20 percent for the next three years, the Semiconductor Industry Association said Monday.

A weakening of the Japanese yen and European currencies against the dollar caused the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics group to nearly halve its growth forecast for this year from 9 percent in real terms, the SIA said.

The midyear forcast is consistent with the industry's average annual growth rate of 17 percent since 1959, the industry group said, with total chip sales worldwide forecast to hit $245.7 billion in the year 2000.

"In the longer term, we see robust growth for the chip industry because the world's appetite for electronic devices -- from simple household appliances to digital cellular telephones and high-end computers -- shows no sign of abating," said Douglas Andrey, SIA information systems and finance director.

The semiconductor industry has grown phenomenally since 1990, when it grew just 1.6 percent as global sales notched up a new annual record of $50.5 billion. By 1995, the growth rate had hit 41.7 percent and sales jumped to $144.4 billion.
Sales fell to $129.2 billion in 1996, however, according to the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) group, an organisation of about 70 chip makers.
